'''Ayana Tamu Arce''' ({{nee}} Holloway) is an American physicist and professor of physics at [[Duke University]]. She works on particle physics, using data from the [[Large Hadron Collider]] to understand phenomena beyond the [[Standard Model]].

== Early life and education ==
Arce was born in [[Lansing, Michigan]]<ref name=":0">{{cite web|last1=Basgall|first1=Monte|title=Tracing Family Threads Toward Superstrings|url=https://today.duke.edu/2010/01/arce.html|website=Duke Today|language=en|date=January 6, 2010}}</ref> and studied physics at [[Princeton University]], graduating with honors and a bachelor's degree in 1998.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://phy.duke.edu/people/ayana-t-arce|title=Ayana T. Arce {{!}} Department of Physics|website=phy.duke.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> 

She moved on to [[Harvard University]] for her PhD, working as the [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|Collider Detector at the Fermilab]] (CDF) detector at [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory|the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> She completed her PhD in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://aawip.com/ayana-holloway-arce/|title=Ayana Holloway-Arce – AAWIP|website=aawip.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref>

== Family ==
Her mother, [[Karla F.C. Holloway|Karla]], is James B. Duke Professor of English and Law at [[Duke University]], with special interest in African American culture. Her father, Russell Holloway, is a computer scientist and [[Duke University Pratt School of Engineering|Pratt School of Engineering]]'s Associate Dean for Corporate and Industrial Relations.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2010-01-06 |title=Tracing Family Threads Toward Superstrings |url=https://today.duke.edu/2010/01/arce.html |access-date=2024-01-12 |website=Duke Today |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
After her Ph.D., Arce completed a Chamberlain post-doctoral fellowship at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], where she worked on experimental techniques to measure the properties of heavy unstable particles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phy.duke.edu/news/ayana-arce-heps-newest-faculty-member|title=Ayana Arce: HEP's Newest Faculty Member {{!}} Department of Physics|website=phy.duke.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> Arce joined [[Duke University]] in 2010 and was made a [[Woodrow Wilson Foundation]] Fellow in 2012.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://woodrow.org/about/fellows/arce-ayana/|title=Woodrow Wilson National Fellowship Foundation {{!}} Arce, Ayana|website=woodrow.org|language=en|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> Arce is working on the [[Calorimeter (particle physics)|calorimeter]] detector at the [[ATLAS experiment]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.learner.org/courses/physics/scientist/transcripts/arce.html|title=Interview - Ayana Arce|website=learner.org|access-date=2018-05-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043759/https://www.learner.org/courses/physics/scientist/transcripts/arce.html|archive-date=2019-03-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/july-2015/something-goes-bump-in-the-data|title=Something goes bump in the data|work=symmetry magazine|access-date=2018-05-12|language=en}}</ref> She is working on jet substructure reconstruction, and the use of jet tagging in [[diboson resonances]].<ref>{{Cite In 2017 Arce and her mother, [[Karla F.C. Holloway|Karla]], were involved in [[Duke University]]'s commemorations of 50 years of Black faculty scholarship.<ref>{{Citation|last=Trinity College Duke|title=Generations: A Conversation with Karla Holloway, Ph.D. & Ayana Arce, Ph.D.|date=2017-12-05|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MUKiyWjLk28|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> She was excited by the film ''[[Hidden Figures]]'' and has taken part in national discussions looking at how to engage more people of colour in scientific careers.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://home.cern/cern-people/updates/2017/03/hidden-figures-light|title=Hidden Figures into the light {{!}} CERN|website=home.cern|language=en|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Duke University|title=Duke Physicist Reflects on Success of "Hidden Figures"|date=2017-02-23|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T0HwATRgNeI|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> She is part of the [[Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory]] research consortium, which supports undergraduate students to complete summer research projects in nuclear and particle physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1757783|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1757783 - REU Site: Undergraduate Research in Nuclear and Particle Physics at TUNL/Duke University|website=nsf.gov|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref>
